topics.name: Whole numbers
subtopics: Revise ordering and comparing whole numbers, properties of operations and calculations using all operations
Calculation techniques: long division, adding, subtracting and multiplying in columns, estimation, rounding off and compensating
Use a calculator only to check the correctness of answers
List prime factors of numbers to at least 3-digit whole numbers
Find the LCM and HCF of whole numbers by inspection or factorisation
Solve problems involving ratio, rate and sharing in a given ratio where the whole is given
Financial contexts: profit, loss, discount, budgets, accounts, loans and simple interest

topics.name: Formal assessment: Assignment (whole numbers)
subtopics: Assignment on whole numbers, done in class over 2 hours

topics.name: Common fractions
subtopics: Order, compare and simplify common fractions, extended to thousandths
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers where one denominator is not a multiple of the other
Multiply common fractions and mixed numbers, not limited to denominators that are multiples of each other
Convert mixed numbers to common fractions to calculate; use multiples and factors to simplify before or after calculating
Use equivalent fractions to add and subtract common fractions
Percentages: calculate the percentage of part of a whole and percentage increase or decrease of whole numbers
Solve problems involving common fractions and mixed numbers (grouping, sharing, fractions of whole numbers) and percentages

topics.name: Decimal fractions
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in decimal fractions to at least 3 decimal places; place value to at least 3 decimal places
Order and compare decimal fractions to at least 3 decimal places; round off to at least 2 decimal places
Add and subtract decimal fractions of at least 3 decimal places
Multiply decimal fractions (3 decimal places) by whole numbers and (2 decimal places) by decimal fractions (1 decimal place)
Divide decimal fractions to at least 3 decimal places by whole numbers
Use place value to estimate the number of decimal places in a result; use rounding off and a calculator to check results
Solve problems in context involving decimal fractions
Equivalence between common fraction, decimal fraction and percentage forms of the same number

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Revision of Term 1 topics

topics.name: Formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Test on all Term 1 topics

sba: Assignment: whole numbers (done in class over 2 hours)

topics.name: Exponents
subtopics: Mental calculations: squares to at least 12² and their square roots; cubes to at least 6³ and their cube roots
Compare and represent whole numbers in exponential form: a^b = a × a × a × … for b factors
Recognise and use the appropriate laws of operations with numbers involving exponents and square and cube roots
Calculations with all four operations using numbers in exponential form (exponents up to 5) and square and cube roots

topics.name: Integers
subtopics: Count forwards and backwards in integers for any interval
Recognise, order and compare integers
Add and subtract with integers
Recognise and use commutative and associative properties of addition for integers

topics.name: Numeric and geometric patterns
subtopics: Investigate and extend numeric and geometric patterns represented in physical or diagram form, in tables, or of learners' own creation
Patterns not limited to sequences involving a constant difference or ratio
Describe and justify the general rules for observed relationships between numbers in own words

topics.name: Functions and relationships
subtopics: Determine input values, output values or rules for patterns and relationships using flow diagrams, tables and formulae
Determine, interpret and justify equivalence of descriptions of the same relationship presented verbally, in flow diagrams, in tables, by formulae and by number sentences

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Revision of Term 1 and Term 2 topics

topics.name: Formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Test on all Term 1 and Term 2 topics

sba: Investigation: on any ONE of the Term 2 topics, administered before teaching it

topics.name: Construction of geometric figures
subtopics: Use a protractor to measure and classify angles: acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex
Construct angles (to one degree of accuracy), parallel lines and perpendicular lines with compass, ruler and protractor
Describe and name parts of a circle

topics.name: Geometry of straight lines
subtopics: Define line segment, ray, straight line, parallel lines and perpendicular lines

topics.name: Geometry of 2D shapes
subtopics: Describe, sort, name and compare triangles by sides and angles: equilateral, isosceles and right-angled
Describe, sort, name and compare quadrilaterals by length of sides, parallel and perpendicular sides and size of angles
Recognise and describe similar and congruent figures by comparing shape and size
Solve simple geometric problems involving unknown sides and angles in triangles and quadrilaterals using known properties

topics.name: Transformation geometry
subtopics: Recognise, describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations with figures on squared paper
Identify and draw lines of symmetry in geometric figures
Draw enlargements and reductions on squared paper and compare them in terms of shape and size

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Revision of Term 3 topics

topics.name: Formal assessment: Test
subtopics: Test on all Term 3 topics

sba: Project: covers a combination of topics from Term 1 to Term 3; completed before the end of Term 3

topics.name: Area and perimeter of 2D shapes
subtopics: Calculate the perimeter of regular and irregular polygons
Use formulae to calculate perimeter and area of squares, rectangles and triangles
Solve problems involving perimeter and area of polygons, calculating to at least 1 decimal place
Use and convert between SI units: mm² ↔ cm², cm² ↔ m²

topics.name: Surface area and volume of 3D objects
subtopics: Use formulae to calculate surface area, volume and capacity of cubes and rectangular prisms
Describe the interrelationship between surface area and volume of cubes and rectangular prisms
Solve problems involving surface area, volume and capacity
Convert between SI units: mm² ↔ cm², cm² ↔ m², mm³ ↔ cm³, cm³ ↔ m³
Use equivalences 1 cm³ ↔ 1 ml and 1 m³ ↔ 1 kl when solving problems

topics.name: Data handling
subtopics: Collect data: pose questions on social, economic and environmental issues; select sources; distinguish samples and populations (learners may be provided with data to save time)
Design and use simple questionnaires with yes/no and multiple-choice responses
Organise and record data using tally marks, tables and stem-and-leaf displays; group data into intervals
Summarise ungrouped numerical data using mean, median and mode; determine the range
Draw bar graphs, double bar graphs, histograms with given intervals and pie charts by hand or technology
Critically read, interpret and analyse data in words, bar graphs, double bar graphs, pie charts and histograms (categories, sources, central tendencies, scales)
Report data: draw conclusions, make predictions, identify sources of error and bias, choose appropriate summary statistics

topics.name: Revision
subtopics: Revision of all topics from Terms 1 to 4

topics.name: Formal assessment: Examination
subtopics: Examination Paper 1 and Paper 2 on all topics from Terms 1 to 4
